# Fixture manifest (TEST-002)

Every fixture file's provenance and the toolchain revision it was
validated under, per TEST-002's own wording. This repo's own CI tracks
the live upstream `sv0-toolchain` default branch (unpinned — see
README's "Deviations from SPEC.md" #2 and `scripts/ci`'s own comment),
so "the toolchain revision" below means the revision each row was
GENERATED/VERIFIED against, not a permanent guarantee the values hold
unchanged forever — `test/unit/`'s own suite (TEST-001) is what
actually re-validates these functions on every CI run; these fixture
files are the discrete, named, boundary-focused complement to that
suite and to `docs/accuracy.md`'s own full-domain ULP sweep.

| File | Provenance | Toolchain revision validated under | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rounding.csv` | Hand-derived from the mathematical definition of floor/ceil/round(half-away-from-zero)/trunc — every value is exact (no floating-point computation needed to derive the EXPECTED column; these are elementary arithmetic facts about where an exact-decimal input falls relative to the nearest integers). ARITH-005 explicitly names this file. | `sv0-toolchain` `43ee2b0` / `sv0c` `d0fa706` | Covers the exact boundary cases ARITH-005's own wording names (`0.0`, `-0.0`, `0.5`, `-0.5`, `2.5`, `-2.5`) plus values adjacent to an integer boundary, a fully-integer value past the 2^52 "already exact" threshold, and `NaN`/`+Infinity`/`-Infinity` propagation. |
| `trig.csv` | Generated by directly calling each function from a standalone C harness compiled against this library's own `sv0`-emitted C (the same technique `docs/ulp_audit_harness.c` uses), at hand-picked domain-boundary/special-value inputs — NOT from `docs/accuracy.md`'s own broad domain sweep (that sweep measures ULP error across a dense grid; this file names a handful of DISCRETE, individually-significant points and their exact or near-exact expected values). Exact endpoints (`asin_f64(1.0)`, `atan_f64(0.0)`, etc.) use the literal double closest to the true mathematical value, transcribed from the harness's own `%.20g`-precision output. | `sv0-toolchain` `43ee2b0` / `sv0c` `d0fa706`, cross-checked against a fresh build at `sv0-toolchain` `c318513` / `sv0c` `53de895` (the revision `scripts/ci`'s own unpinned GitHub Actions workflow picked up) | Building this file directly found and fixed two real bugs in `lib/trig.sv0`/`lib/arith.sv0`: `sqrt_f64(+Infinity)` and `exp_f64(-Infinity)` were both silently computing `NaN` (not `Infinity`/`0.0` as IEEE-754 requires) before their `ensures` clauses caught it — see `BUGS.md`'s "Working today" section / `lib/trig.sv0`'s own comments on `sqrt_f64`/`exp_f64` for the full writeup. Also found and fixed a latent gap in `abs_f64`'s own `ensures` (didn't have a `NaN` escape hatch, so `abs_f64(NaN)` — an IEEE-754-correct `NaN` result — panicked on its own contract). `sqrt_f64(-1.0)`/`sqrt_f64(NaN)` intentionally recorded as `PANIC` rows (not `NaN`-propagating) — see the CSV's own notes column for why this is a real, open, documented ambiguity (CONV-005(a) vs (b)), not a mistake in this fixture file. |

## Schema

`rounding.csv`: `input,floor_expected,ceil_expected,round_expected,trunc_expected,category,notes` — one row tests all four rounding functions at once against the same input.

`trig.csv`: `function,input1,input2,expected,tolerance,category,notes` — `input2` is empty for single-argument functions (everything except `atan2_f64`). `expected` is either a literal double, `PANIC` (the row documents a `requires`-violation case, not a return value), or `nan`/`inf`/`-inf` (compared via `is_nan_f64`/`is_infinite_f64`-style checks, not `==`, since `NaN != NaN` by definition). `category` values: `boundary`, `neg_zero`, `nan`, `infinity`, `near_integer`, `typical` — TEST-003's own "domain-boundary and NaN/Infinity/-0.0" wording maps directly onto `boundary`/`neg_zero`/`nan`/`infinity` here.

Both files ARE now wired into a "read the CSV, call the function, compare" runner: **`scripts/run_fixture_parity.py`** generates one `fn main() -> i32` with a check per (row, function) from `rounding.csv` and `trig.csv`, compiles + runs it on BOTH backends (C: native `--project` → `cc` → execute; VM: native VM emitter → `.sv0b` → `sv0vm`), and asserts every result matches the row's own EXPECTED column AND that the C and VM exit codes agree. It runs in `scripts/ci` (the "per-fixture cross-backend value check" step, `--skip-fixture-parity` to skip) and closes the per-fixture surface of COMPAT-002 / TEST-005 — `scripts/check_fixtures.py` still separately lints the tables for completeness/boundary coverage (TEST-002/TEST-003). Notes on what the runner does and does not gate:

- **Sign of a zero result is not distinguished.** `ceil_f64`/`trunc_f64` of a small negative input return `+0.0` in this library where C's libm returns `-0.0`; SPEC.md pins no sign-of-zero for those, so the runner compares zero results by value only (the `-0.0` cells in `rounding.csv` still document the intended magnitude). What it does gate is that both backends agree and both match the fixture value.
- **`PANIC` rows are listed as skipped** — a `requires`-violation can't be exercised inside one non-crashing binary; those rows document a contract, not a return value.
- The generated program is staged into a throwaway `--project` dir and never committed; run `scripts/run_fixture_parity.py --emit-only <path>` to inspect it.
